article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 60% Sativa / 40% Indica
Genetics: Amnesia Haze × Lemon Skunk
Breeder: Barney’s Farm
THC Content: 26%
CBD Content: 1% or less
Terpene Profile: Limonene , terpinolene, caryophyllene
Primary Flavors: Lemon, sweet citrus, spice, earth, Skunk
Flowering Time (Indoor): 60–65 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: First to second week of October
Indoor Yield: 500–600 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 800 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Easy to moderate

Amnesia Lemon belongs to a select group of cannabis strains whose name tells only half the story. Lemon certainly dominates the first encounter, arriving as fresh peel, citrus oil, and sharp zest, but underneath sits the incense-like depth, earthy spice, and soaring cerebral character inherited from Amnesia Haze. Barney’s Farm developed this cultivar after obtaining a prized Amnesia Haze selection from Soma and crossing it with Lemon Skunk, turning two celebrated European cannabis influences into a quicker-flowering, more manageable hybrid.

The result preserves much of the mental intensity associated with Haze while shortening the production cycle to roughly nine weeks and keeping indoor plants around one meter tall. THC levels now reach approximately 26%, giving the flower considerably more strength than its bright, approachable citrus aroma might suggest. For growers who enjoy sativa-oriented weed but dislike extremely tall plants and 12-week flowering schedules, Amnesia Lemon offers an unusually practical route into classic Haze character.
Genetics and Lineage

The genetic foundation combines Amnesia Haze with Lemon Skunk, and the history behind that pairing is important. Soma’s Amnesia Haze became one of the defining varieties of the Amsterdam cannabis scene , earning recognition for an intensely cerebral effect, exotic aroma, and complex Haze expression. Amnesia Haze itself carries a broad genetic background associated with Haze, Southeast Asian, Jamaican, and Afghan-influenced cannabis, which helps explain its mixture of tropical, spicy, earthy, and incense-like qualities. After Barney’s Farm gained access to a particularly desirable Amnesia Haze phenotype, that selection became the foundation for Amnesia Lemon.

Lemon Skunk was chosen as the other parent for good reason. Skunk genetics contribute vigor, sturdy flower development, reliable production, and a shorter bloom period than traditional Haze plants . Lemon-selected Skunk lines intensify sharp citrus terpenes while retaining the pungent sweetness and earthy depth that made classic Skunk marijuana so influential. Crossing the two parents therefore solved several practical problems at once: the Lemon Skunk side improved speed and manageability while reinforcing citrus aroma, and the Amnesia Haze parent preserved the soaring mental quality and exotic complexity breeders wanted to retain.

The completed hybrid is approximately 60% sativa and 40% indica. That relatively close balance is visible throughout the plant. Growth remains upright and vigorous without becoming uncontrollably tall, flowers develop into long but reasonably dense colas, and the effects begin with unmistakable cerebral stimulation before a softer physical calm develops later. Rather than functioning as a diluted Amnesia Haze, the cross creates a distinct cultivar with its own combination of Haze intensity, Skunk practicality, and unusually concentrated lemon flavor.
Effects and Experience

The experience generally begins quickly and unmistakably in the head. Thoughts can become more active, sensory details feel sharper, and a noticeable improvement in mood may develop before the body changes very much. At moderate doses, the mental quality is energetic rather than scattered, making conversation, music, writing, art, gaming, or exploratory activities particularly appealing. Some consumers find that ordinary tasks become easier to engage with simply because attention feels more interested in the moment. This is one reason Amnesia Lemon has remained popular with people who prefer marijuana that contributes energy rather than immediately slowing the day down.

As the initial cerebral wave settles, the 40% indica influence becomes easier to recognize. The body relaxes gradually without necessarily becoming heavy, smoothing out some of the sharper edges of the Haze experience. That secondary calm distinguishes the strain from more extreme sativas that remain intensely stimulating for hours. Used conservatively, it can fit daytime or early-evening situations in which the consumer wants to remain social and mentally present while still enjoying noticeable physical ease.

High doses tell a different story. At roughly 26% THC, this cultivar is capable of producing strong psychoactivity, and the energetic mental side can become uncomfortable if consumed carelessly. Racing thoughts, temporary anxiety, dry mouth, dry eyes, or dizziness are possible, particularly for people who are sensitive to THC-rich sativa weed. Larger servings may eventually become heavier as the experience matures, but waiting for that relaxation after overconsumption can be unpleasant. Experienced consumers generally get the clearest expression of the genetics by keeping the dose moderate enough to preserve the uplifting Haze character.
Medical Benefits

For medical cannabis consumers, the most relevant quality may be the combination of mental stimulation and later physical balance. Some people dealing with daytime fatigue, low motivation, or stress prefer uplifting marijuana because heavily sedating strains can make normal activities more difficult. The early cerebral effect may provide a temporary shift in mood and attention without immediately creating the physical heaviness associated with traditional nighttime indicas. Individual responses vary substantially, however, and stimulating THC can aggravate nervousness in susceptible patients.

Pain and muscular tension may become more manageable as the later relaxation develops. THC acts through cannabinoid receptors and additional neurological pathways involved in pain perception, while the modest body component can make persistent discomfort feel less intrusive without necessarily producing immediate couch-lock. Appetite may also increase in some consumers. Because CBD levels are low, Amnesia Lemon should not be considered a balanced cannabinoid cultivar; the medical experience is largely driven by THC and the wider chemical profile of the flower.

Limonene, terpinolene, beta-caryophyllene, and myrcene are commonly associated with its aroma. Limonene creates much of the citrus brightness, terpinolene can contribute floral, piney, fruity, and herbal complexity, caryophyllene supplies peppery spice, and myrcene deepens the earthy background. These compounds are biologically active and remain subjects of cannabis research, but a terpene list cannot reliably predict an individual medical response. Patients using marijuana therapeutically should pay attention to the laboratory analysis of the specific batch, personal tolerance, medication interactions, and guidance from an appropriate healthcare professional when necessary.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Fresh lemon peel dominates the first impression. Properly cured flowers can release an almost oily citrus scent when broken apart, reminiscent of squeezing zest directly from the rind rather than smelling artificial lemon candy. Sweetness sits immediately behind the acidity, while earth, herbs, and mild Skunk pungency begin to surface after the initial citrus rush. Haze ancestry adds another layer that may resemble incense, exotic spice, flowers, or dry wood depending on the phenotype.

Limonene naturally supports the lemon and citrus-oil qualities, while terpinolene gives the bouquet a more elusive combination of fresh fruit, herbs, pine, and floral sweetness. Caryophyllene introduces pepper and dry spice, and myrcene can deepen the base with earth and musk. The balance changes from plant to plant. Some expressions are intensely lemon-forward, whereas others show more Haze spice and earthy Skunk character beneath the fruit.

On the palate, tart lemon usually appears first before moving toward sweeter citrus through the middle of the inhale. The finish becomes noticeably more complex, introducing spice, earth, and a faintly musky Skunk quality. Vaporization often preserves the brightest citrus notes, while combustion brings the deeper herbal and spicy side forward. A patient cure is particularly important because the most volatile lemon compounds disappear quickly from overdried weed, leaving a much flatter profile that fails to capture what makes the cultivar distinctive.
Growing Information

Amnesia Lemon provides many of the traits growers want from a sativa-dominant plant without the logistical problems associated with extreme Haze genetics. Indoors, plants generally finish around 100–110 centimeters, while outdoor specimens commonly reach roughly 120–150 centimeters. Growth is upright with enough lateral branching to support multiple productive flowering sites. The plant can stretch after the light cycle changes, but the expansion remains far easier to manage than a tropical sativa capable of tripling or quadrupling in height.

Topping and low-stress training work well when growers want to spread growth across a wider canopy. A Screen of Green can be especially effective because the branches are flexible enough to guide horizontally before they harden during flowering. Removing weak lower shoots helps direct energy toward the long upper colas and improves airflow through the interior. Indoor flowering generally takes about 60–65 days, remarkably fast considering the Amnesia Haze influence. Under optimized lighting and environmental conditions, production can reach approximately 500–600 grams per square meter.

Outdoors, plants can produce up to roughly 800 grams each in favorable conditions and generally finish during the first or second week of October. Full sun, ample root space, consistent irrigation, and warm conditions through late summer support the highest yields. Long colas require good air movement as they gain density, particularly in humid autumn climates. Growers should monitor rainfall and flower moisture closely as harvest approaches rather than assuming Haze-influenced buds are automatically resistant to mold. Resin production becomes substantial during the final weeks, making mature material useful not only as flower but also for dry sift, hash, and rosin when terpene preservation is handled carefully.
FAQ
What strains make Amnesia Lemon?

Amnesia Lemon is a cross between Amnesia Haze and Lemon Skunk. Barney’s Farm developed the cultivar using a selected Amnesia Haze phenotype supplied through its collaboration with Soma. Lemon Skunk contributes citrus intensity, vigor, and a shorter flowering period, while Amnesia Haze supplies the cerebral effect and exotic Haze character.
Is Amnesia Lemon indica or sativa?

The cultivar is approximately 60% sativa and 40% indica. Its mental effects and growth pattern lean clearly toward the sativa side, producing an uplifting, cerebral experience and relatively elongated colas. The indica component adds enough structure and physical relaxation to keep the plant and high more manageable than a traditional pure Haze.
How much THC is in Amnesia Lemon?

Current Barney’s Farm material lists approximately 26% THC. Earlier breeder catalogs documented lower figures around 21%, illustrating how breeder selections, cultivation techniques, and testing standards can change reported potency over time. Actual harvested flower may vary according to phenotype, environment, maturity, curing, storage, and laboratory methodology.
What does Amnesia Lemon taste like?

Fresh lemon and sweet citrus dominate the flavor, followed by spice, earth, herbs, and mild Skunk pungency. Haze-oriented phenotypes may also reveal incense, floral, or woody qualities. Limonene is strongly associated with the citrus profile, while terpinolene, caryophyllene, and myrcene contribute additional complexity.
How long does Amnesia Lemon take to flower?

Indoor flowering generally requires approximately 60–65 days, or around eight and a half to nine weeks. Outdoors, harvest normally falls during the first or second week of October in favorable Northern Hemisphere climates. Trichome development, flower maturity, plant health, and local weather should still determine the final harvest date.
Final Thoughts on Amnesia Lemon

Amnesia Lemon occupies an unusual position among Haze-derived cannabis. It preserves much of the mental lift, aromatic complexity, and cerebral intensity that made Amnesia Haze famous while removing some of the cultivation inconveniences traditionally associated with long-flowering sativas. Lemon Skunk shortens the cycle, reinforces the citrus aroma, and contributes enough structure to keep indoor plants close to a meter tall.

The sensory profile is equally successful. Lemon peel and citrus oil dominate without erasing the earth, spice, incense, and Skunk qualities underneath. That contrast creates a flavor more sophisticated than simple lemon sweetness and provides a clear connection to both parents. Effects move through a similar progression, beginning energetic and mentally engaging before settling into a smoother physical state.

For growers, 60–65 days of flowering, indoor yields approaching 600 g/m², manageable height, and outdoor production around 800 grams per plant create an attractive combination of speed and productivity. For consumers, approximately 26% THC ensures that the strain remains powerful enough for experienced users despite its bright flavor and upbeat personality.

More than anything, Amnesia Lemon demonstrates how successful breeding can preserve the defining character of a famous parent while making the resulting plant easier to cultivate. It remains a strong choice for anyone seeking citrus-heavy marijuana with genuine Haze heritage, high potency, energetic effects, and a flowering cycle short enough to fit comfortably into a modern grow room.
